rv.q: The undertaking, although a bit uneven in some ways, is successful on the whole in being both celebratory and thought-provoking.
Everything about 1619: The Journey Of A People works.
The staging by Williams and Fleetwood-Jourdain producing artistic director Tim Rhoze is most emotionally effective in the wordless dance and movement sections.

I wouldn’t necessarily call 1619 inspirational , but … let’s say it’s a safe production to recommend to your more ‘un-woke’ friends with reasonable confidence that they will learn something without being scared away.
“1619: The Journey of a People” offers a concise history of the Black American experience in an easy-to-digest formula—with a few surprises thrown in.

cn.t: Critics praise *1619: The Journey of a People* as a powerful, propulsive journey through Black American history. Ted Williams III's blend of music, dance, and spoken word—anchored by a stunning visual design—earns strong acclaim as both celebratory and thought-provoking.
